author: Arthur Security <security@arthur.ai>
_comment: Scope: HIGH/CRITICAL findings that a container-image re-scan still reports for the genai-engine, ml-engine and genai-engine-models-* images AND that are not exploitable in our usage. Every statement here is 'not_affected' with a justification. Remediated CVEs are excluded by policy — fix, don't justify (security/README.md), so a CVE disappearing from this document means it was fixed, not dropped. Remediated and therefore absent: python3.11 is removed from every image (its dpkg metadata deleted); litellm/langsmith/msgpack/nltk/uv/pyasn1 are upgraded past their advisories; libexpat1 is at 2.5.0-1+deb12u4 in every image as of 2026-10-02, which fixes CVE-2026-45186, CVE-2025-59375, CVE-2026-25210 and CVE-2026-66046, so their statements were removed; models-gcs is rebuilt with perl-base 5.36.0-7+deb12u4 and libpcre2-8-0 10.42-1+deb12u2 as of 2026-10-05, which fix CVE-2026-42496, CVE-2026-42497, CVE-2026-48962, CVE-2026-8376, CVE-2026-13221, CVE-2026-57433, CVE-2026-57432 and CVE-2026-103111, so their statements were removed (perl CVE-2026-9538 is still unfixed in bookworm and keeps its statement); and as of 2026-07-30 the distroless OS-package findings (libc6, libssl3, libkrb5*, liblzma5) are fixed at the source — the build stages now mirror the base's /lib layout with their apt-upgraded libraries and rewrite /var/lib/dpkg/status.d to the versions actually installed, so the patched objects ship and scanners read true versions. Auditor note: the distroless base is not merged-/usr, so before that change `COPY /usr/lib` never reached the glibc and liblzma objects the base keeps in /lib. Images up to and including 2.1.754 shipped the base's unpatched glibc (2.36-9+deb12u13) and liblzma5 (5.4.1-1), and earlier revisions of this document incorrectly recorded those libc6 CVEs as fixed. The libssl3 and krb5 objects do live under /usr/lib and were genuinely patched throughout; only their dpkg metadata was stale. See genai-engine/dockerfile, ml-engine/Dockerfile, deployment/model-upload/Dockerfile and PR #2073. Audited 2026-08-18 against the per-image Trivy reports from the daily image-vuln-scan: (a) no remaining statement suppresses a finding that has an upstream fix — every one is unfixed at the installed version, so none is masking a bump we could take instead; (b) the python3.11 statements (CVE-2025-69534, CVE-2026-3644, CVE-2026-4224, CVE-2026-6100, CVE-2026-7210, CVE-2025-13836) were removed because the runtime-s3 and runtime-fs stages now delete the interpreter and its dpkg metadata outright, so the packages are absent and those statements matched nothing; (c) the document is scoped to HIGH/CRITICAL, so four statements were removed for falling below that line: CVE-2026-11822 and CVE-2026-11824 (libsqlite3-0) and CVE-2026-56131 and CVE-2026-56407 (libexpat1) were re-rated from HIGH to MEDIUM in the vulnerability database. Note what this does and does not mean: those four are NOT remediated. The packages are still installed at the same versions and Debian still ships no fix (it marks the sqlite pair <postponed> for bookworm); they simply sit under the scan's --severity HIGH,CRITICAL filter, so nothing reports them today. If any of them is ever re-rated back to HIGH it will surface as an untriaged finding and will need its justification restored -- the reasoning was sound, only the severity changed. Updated 2026-10-28 against the daily Trivy reports for 2.1.1073-dev and an external scan of 2.1.980: CVE-2026-84782 (libssl3) was removed because bookworm-security now ships the fix in 3.0.22-1~deb12u2. genai-engine-cpu/gpu and ml-engine already carry it; the models images had been re-tagged rather than rebuilt and are rebuilt by this change. CVE-2026-81726 (nltk) was removed because nltk 3.10.4, now shipped, contains the upstream fix (commit 303f6e2), even though the advisory still lists no patched version. Fixed rather than justified: aiohttp, Authlib, brotli, certifi, oauthlib, pillow, virtualenv and uv (0.13.6, GHSA-hq85-5cpj-mr62), plus filelock in the models images. Added: CVE-2026-112940 (filelock, capped below 4.0 by litellm), CVE-2026-72848 (langchain-community, no fix), CVE-2026-115506 (libexpat1, no fix) and CVE-2026-85091 (zlib1g, version not affected).

statements._comment: zlib1g: The overflow is in MiniZip (zlib contrib/minizip), which upstream states is not a supported part of zlib. Debian's zlib1g shared library does not build or export the MiniZip code (the vulnerable zipOpenNewFileInZip4_64 symbol is absent); Arthur links only the core inflate/deflate API. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2026-12-27.
statements.impact_statement: The overflow is in MiniZip (zlib contrib/minizip), which upstream states is not a supported part of zlib. Debian's zlib1g shared library does not build or export the MiniZip code (the vulnerable zipOpenNewFileInZip4_64 symbol is absent); Arthur links only the core inflate/deflate API.

statements._comment: ncurses: The buffer overflow is in the infocmp CLI / terminfo handling. The images run a non-interactive service with no TTY; Arthur never invokes infocmp nor renders attacker-controlled terminal/terminfo data. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2026-12-27.
statements.impact_statement: The buffer overflow is in the infocmp CLI / terminfo handling. The images run a non-interactive service with no TTY; Arthur never invokes infocmp nor renders attacker-controlled terminal/terminfo data.

statements._comment: libsqlite3-0: Persistence uses PostgreSQL (pgvector); libsqlite3 is a transitive dependency that is never given attacker-controlled SQL. Exploitation requires executing crafted SQL (KeyInfoFromExprList), which is not in the engine's data path. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2026-12-27.
statements.impact_statement: Persistence uses PostgreSQL (pgvector); libsqlite3 is a transitive dependency that is never given attacker-controlled SQL. Exploitation requires executing crafted SQL (KeyInfoFromExprList), which is not in the engine's data path.

statements._comment: util-linux (libblkid1 and sibling packages): CVE-2026-53615 is an integer overflow in libblkid's DOS/MBR partition parser (partitions/dos.c, parse_dos_extended); no Debian bookworm fix is available (bookworm ships 2.38.1-5+deb12u3, still vulnerable; Debian bug #1140197). Triggering requires libblkid to probe an attacker-controlled block device / disk image / partition table. These images never probe disks or mount untrusted media — the engines are network services and the model-upload job only downloads model files and writes to cloud storage / a mounted volume. Subcomponents are name-only so the statement matches whichever util-linux binary packages a given image ships (distroless images carry only libuuid1; the slim models-gcs runtime carries the full set). Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-01-28.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-53615 is an integer overflow in libblkid's DOS/MBR partition-table parser (partitions/dos.c). It is reachable only when libblkid probes an attacker-controlled block device, disk image, or partition table. These images never probe disks or mount untrusted media: the engines are network services and the model-upload job only downloads model files and writes them to cloud storage / a mounted volume. No Debian bookworm fix is available yet.

statements._comment: libacl1: CVE-2026-54369 is a symlink-traversal privilege escalation in libacl's pathname-based functions (acl_get_file/acl_set_file/acl_extended_file/acl_delete_def_file follow symlinks); no Debian bookworm fix is available (bookworm ships acl 2.3.1-3, no-dsa/postponed; fixed upstream in acl 2.4.0). Exploitation requires a local unprivileged attacker racing a higher-privileged process that operates on ACLs of attacker-controllable paths. The models-gcs image runs a single non-interactive Python entrypoint (upload_models.py) as one user with no other local users and performs no ACL operations on untrusted paths. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-01-28.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-54369 is a local symlink-traversal privilege escalation in libacl's pathname-based functions. It requires a local unprivileged attacker and a higher-privileged process performing ACL operations on attacker-controllable paths. The models-gcs image runs a single non-interactive Python entrypoint (upload_models.py) as one user, has no other local users, and performs no ACL operations on untrusted paths. No Debian bookworm fix is available yet (fixed upstream in acl 2.4.0).

statements._comment: gzip: CVE-2026-41992 is a global buffer overflow (OOB read) from improperly reused global state between the LZW and LZH decoders in a single gzip invocation; no Debian bookworm fix is available (bookworm ships gzip 1.12-1, no-dsa/postponed). Triggering requires feeding gzip a crafted LZW file followed by a crafted LZH file in one command. The models-gcs image never invokes gzip on attacker-controlled .lzw/.lzh archives — the upload job downloads model files and writes them to cloud storage. gzip is a transitive base-OS package. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-01-28.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-41992 is an out-of-bounds read from reused global state between gzip's LZW and LZH decoders, triggered only by decompressing a crafted LZW file followed by a crafted LZH file in a single gzip invocation. The models-gcs image never invokes gzip on attacker-controlled archives; gzip is a transitive base-OS package and the upload job only downloads model files and writes them to cloud storage. No Debian bookworm fix is available yet.

statements._comment: openssl/libssl3: CVE-2026-14456 is unbounded memory growth in the OpenSSL QUIC SERVER incoming-channel queue (a listener queues an unlimited number of pending channels for Initial packets with unknown connection IDs). Upstream OpenSSL rates it LOW and lists the affected ranges as >=3.5.0 <3.5.8, >=3.6.0 <3.6.4 and >=4.0.0 <4.0.2 — the QUIC server implementation was only added in 3.5. Every Arthur image ships OpenSSL 3.0.20-1~deb12u2, which predates that code entirely, so the vulnerable function is not present in the shipped object. Trivy reports it because Debian's tracker has not yet triaged the CVE and defaults every openssl branch to 'vulnerable' (it likewise marks bullseye's 1.1.1w vulnerable, which cannot be true for a 3.5-era feature); that is also why the report shows no fixed version. Nothing in these images runs a QUIC listener in any case. Re-check once Debian triages bookworm; if 3.0.x is ever shown to contain the queueing code this must be revisited. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-02-18.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-14456 affects the OpenSSL QUIC server listener, which was introduced in OpenSSL 3.5. Upstream lists the affected ranges as >=3.5.0 <3.5.8, >=3.6.0 <3.6.4 and >=4.0.0 <4.0.2, and rates the issue LOW. These images ship OpenSSL 3.0.20-1~deb12u2, in which the QUIC server implementation does not exist, so the vulnerable code is not present in the shipped library. No Arthur process operates a QUIC listener regardless. No Debian fix is listed because bookworm's 3.0.x branch was never affected.

statements._comment: libsqlite3-0: CVE-2026-11822 is arbitrary code execution via crafted FTS5 full-text search data. Justification restored — this statement was removed on 2026-08-18 only because the CVE had been re-rated HIGH to MEDIUM and fell below this document's severity scope; it has since been re-rated back to HIGH and resurfaced as an untriaged finding, exactly as that audit note anticipated. The reasoning is unchanged: persistence uses PostgreSQL (pgvector), libsqlite3 is a transitive dependency that is never given attacker-controlled SQL, and the engines never use FTS5. Debian marks the sqlite3 pair postponed for bookworm, so no fix is available at 3.40.1-2+deb12u2. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-03-02.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-11822 requires supplying crafted FTS5 full-text search data to SQLite. Persistence uses PostgreSQL (pgvector); libsqlite3 is a transitive dependency that is never given attacker-controlled SQL, and no FTS5 functionality is used. No Debian bookworm fix is available (postponed).

Justification restored — removed on 2026-08-18 only for falling below the HIGH/CRITICAL scope after a HIGH to MEDIUM re-rating, and now re-rated back to HIGH. The reasoning is unchanged: persistence uses PostgreSQL (pgvector), libsqlite3 is never given attacker-controlled SQL, and FTS5 is not used. Debian marks the sqlite3 pair postponed for bookworm, so no fix is available at 3.40.1-2+deb12u2. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-03-02.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-11824 is a heap-based buffer overflow reachable only through SQLite's FTS5 module. Persistence uses PostgreSQL (pgvector); libsqlite3 is a transitive dependency that is never given attacker-controlled SQL, and FTS5 is not used. No Debian bookworm fix is available (postponed).

statements._comment: util-linux (libuuid1 and sibling packages): CVE-2026-53613 is a TOCTOU race in the mount program via an ancestor-directory swap on the target path. Bookworm ships 2.38.1-5+deb12u3 and the security tracker still lists util-linux as open, so no fix is available. This is a sibling of the already-justified CVE-2026-53615 in the same package set at the same version. Exploitation requires invoking mount(8) against a path an adversary can restructure concurrently; these images never call mount at runtime — the engines are network services and the model-upload job only downloads model files and writes to cloud storage or an already-mounted volume. Subcomponents are name-only so the statement matches whichever util-linux binary packages a given image ships (distroless images carry only libuuid1; the slim models-gcs runtime carries the full set). Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-03-02.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-53613 is a TOCTOU race in mount(8) requiring an adversary to swap an ancestor directory of the mount target during the call. These images never invoke mount at runtime: the engines are network services and the model-upload job only downloads model files and writes them to cloud storage / an already-mounted volume. No Debian bookworm fix is available.

statements._comment: libsystemd0 / libudev1: CVE-2026-16742 is reported against systemd 252.39-1~deb12u2 on the models-gcs image, the only image carrying these packages; the Debian security tracker lists systemd as open, so no fix is available. No Arthur process runs systemd, systemd-udevd or any systemd daemon — the images have no init system and the model-upload job runs a single Python entrypoint (upload_models.py). libsystemd0 and libudev1 are present only as transitive shared-library dependencies of other base packages, and their client APIs are never called. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-03-09.

Debian ships no fix at the installed 252.39-1~deb12u2.

statements._comment: filelock: CVE-2026-112940 lets an attacker with rename access to a non-sticky parent directory swap the SQLite database and side files that filelock's ReadWriteLock reopens by name, turning its writes into overwrite/unlink of attacker-chosen files. Fixed in filelock 4.2.1, but genai-engine and ml-engine cannot take it: litellm (pinned by both, and by arthur-common) requires filelock>=3.16.1,<4.0 through the latest release, 1.106.5, so both lockfiles resolve to 3.32.7. The models images are not affected — they do not depend on litellm and ship filelock 4.2.4. Only ReadWriteLock / AsyncReadWriteLock is vulnerable; the plain FileLock / SoftFileLock used by huggingface-hub, torch, transformers, tldextract and virtualenv is not. No package installed in either image and no Arthur code references ReadWriteLock (checked by grepping site-packages), and the images run as a single nonroot user with no other local principal to race the rename. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-04-28, or as soon as litellm accepts filelock>=4.2.1.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-112940 is confined to filelock's SQLite-backed ReadWriteLock. Nothing in these images uses it: Arthur code does not import filelock, and every installed dependency that does (huggingface-hub, torch, transformers, tldextract) uses the unaffected FileLock. Exploitation also requires a second local principal with rename access to the lock's parent directory, which the single-user images do not have. The fixed release (4.2.1) cannot be installed because litellm caps filelock below 4.0.

statements._comment: langchain-community: CVE-2026-72848 is an SSRF in SitemapLoader.parse_sitemap, which applies restrict_to_same_domain to leaf <url> entries but not to nested <sitemap> entries, so an attacker-controlled sitemap can make the server fetch an internal URL. Reported against 0.4.2 (genai-engine/pyproject.toml). The advisory marks every release as affected with no patched version, so there is no upgrade to take. genai-engine never constructs SitemapLoader, WebBaseLoader or any langchain_community document loader (grep of genai-engine/src for SitemapLoader/sitemap finds nothing outside tokenizer vocabularies), so no sitemap is ever fetched or parsed. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-04-28, or as soon as a fixed langchain-community is released.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-72848 is reachable only through langchain-community's SitemapLoader. The engine never instantiates SitemapLoader or any other langchain_community web document loader, so no sitemap is fetched and the missing domain check is never exercised. No patched release exists.

statements._comment: libexpat1: CVE-2026-115506 is a CPU-exhaustion DoS — expat's billion-laughs accounting (accountingDiffTolerated) trips too late, so a moderately sized XML document with a large DTD and nested entities costs tens of seconds of CPU per parse. Reported against 2.5.0-1+deb12u4 by an external scanner; the images now ship 2.5.0-1+deb12u5, and the advisory covers every libexpat through 2.9.0 with no fix, so there is no upgrade to take. No Arthur code parses XML (no xml.*, lxml, defusedxml, ElementTree or pyexpat use in genai-engine/src or ml-engine/src), and no API accepts XML input. The only XML parsed at runtime is cloud SDK response bodies (botocore for S3, Azure SDK) received over TLS from the provider's endpoint, which an attacker cannot author. Impact is bounded CPU on a single request, with no memory corruption or data exposure. models-gcs does not ship libexpat1. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-04-28.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-115506 requires the attacker to supply an XML document with a crafted DTD. No Arthur code or API parses XML; expat is reached only when cloud SDKs parse response bodies received over TLS from the provider's own endpoint, which an attacker cannot control. Impact would be bounded CPU per parse. No fixed libexpat release exists.

statements._comment: zlib1g: CVE-2026-85091 is a heap overflow in gz_vacate() during non-blocking gzwrite()/gzprintf(). The advisory scopes it to zlib 1.3.1.2 through 1.3.2, where the gz_vacate code path was introduced (OSV range starts at upstream commit 570720b). Every image ships Debian bookworm's zlib1g 1:1.2.13.dfsg-1, which predates that code, so the vulnerable function is not present. The scanner flags it only because Debian has not triaged bookworm, which is also why no fixed version is shown. Arthur does not call gzprintf/gzwrite in any case. Owner: security@arthur.ai. Review by: 2027-04-28.
statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-85091 affects only zlib 1.3.1.2 through 1.3.2, in which the vulnerable gz_vacate() code was introduced. These images ship zlib 1.2.13 (Debian 1:1.2.13.dfsg-1), which does not contain that code.
